data.source_title: Factors Associated with Patients Leaving Without Being Seen in a Canadian Emergency Department
data.locator: Abstract; Results; Table, LWBS denominator and adjusted operational factors.
data.source_setting: The Ottawa Hospital General Campus, tertiary-care/cancer-center ED, Canada.
data.source_n: 170,536 ED encounters; 15,473 LWBS; 2,716 left before triage.
data.quantity: LWBS and pre-triage departure shares; adjusted odds change with queue counts
data.unit: encounters; percent; adjusted odds ratio per five people
data.source_evidence_basis: All-encounter retrospective cohort; the paper reports 9.1% in abstract and 9.2% in detailed results (15,473/170,536 is about 9.1%). Pre-triage departures were separately counted. Adjusted odds rose with both waiting-patient and awaiting-disposition counts.
data.limitations: Single Canadian center, observational design; records did not include arrival method and authors did not report downstream outcomes for departures. Percent rounding differs between abstract and detailed text.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Keep registered-but-not-triaged departure and post-triage/pre-physician LWBS as separate absorbing outcomes, linked to queue state. Treat reported associations as external evidence, not transferable departure probabilities.
